{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=non-convex+scalarization+methods+for+multi-objective+reinforcement+learning+and+autonomous+reward+discovery&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.65109/lngi4831\", \"title\": [\"Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Non-Linear Scalarization\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) setup naturally arises in many places where an agent optimizes multiple objectives. We consider the problem of MORL where multiple objectives are combined using a non-linear scalarization. We combine the vector objectives with a concave scalarization function and maximize this scalar objective. To work with the non-linear scalarization, in this paper, we propose a solution using steady-state occupancy measures and long-term average rewards. We show that when the scalarization function is element-wise increasing, the optimal policy for the scalarization is also Pareto optimal. To maximize the scalarized objective, we propose a model-based posterior sampling algorithm. Using a novel Bellman error analysis for infinite horizon MDPs based proof, we show that the proposed algorithm obtains a regret bound of ~O(LKDS√A/T) for K objectives, and L-Lipschitz continous scalarization function for MDP with S states, A actions, and diameter D. Additionally, we propose policy-gradient and actor-critic algorithms for MORL. For the policy gradient actor, we obtain the gradient using chain rule, and we learn different critics for each of the K objectives. Finally, we implement our algorithms on multiple environments including deep-sea treasure, and network scheduling setups to demonstrate that the proposed algorithms can optimize non-linear scalarization of multiple objectives.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.65109/lngi4831\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 5, 9]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-3-319-61007-8_2\", \"title\": [\"Scalarization\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-61007-8_2\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2017]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-pmnmb\", \"title\": [\"The Impact of Reward Scalarization and Weight Scheduling on Optimization Dynamics in Multi-Objective Molecular Design\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Inverse molecular design aims to generate novel chemical structures that satisfy multiple property constraints, yet reinforcement-learning (RL) fine-tuning can be sensitive to how objectives are converted into a scalar reward. Here, we systematically analyze how scalarization choices and stabilization mechanisms shape optimization dynamics in REINVENT-based RL fine-tuning for multi-parameter optimization (MPO).  Using policy gradient techniques such as REINVENT, we evaluate three scalarization schemes—linear (sum), geometric (product), and Chebyshev-type—under multiple target regimes that vary in constraint tightness and prior support. While broad targets yield stable behavior across scalarizations, narrow and weakly supported targets expose sharp failure modes. We further show that target-aware weight scheduling accelerates hypervolume growth and can rescue collapse regimes. Finally, entropy regularization provides an orthogonal safeguard but only in specific cases.   Collectively, our results highlight critical interactions between scalarization choice and weight dynamics, and provide mechanistic insight and actionable guidance for stabilizing RL fine-tuning in constrained molecular MPO.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-pmnmb\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 12, 22]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.71443/9789349552982-13\", \"title\": [\"Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Balancing Efficiency and Safety in Autonomous Decision Making\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This book chapter explores the integration of multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) for balancing efficiency and safety in autonomous decision-making. As autonomous systems are increasingly deployed in complex, real-world environments, ensuring both high-performance optimization and safety becomes paramount. The chapter delves into the fundamental concepts of MORL, emphasizing how multiple conflicting objectives can be addressed simultaneously, while maintaining robust safety standards. Various methods, such as risk-sensitive learning, safety constraints, and reward shaping, are examined to effectively guide autonomous agents in navigating trade-offs between exploration and safety. Additionally, the chapter discusses policy-based methods, verification, and validation techniques crucial for real-world implementation. With a focus on real-world testing for safety assurance, it presents strategies for integrating safety-critical components in decision-making processes. This work provides valuable insights into enhancing the reliability, performance, and safety of autonomous systems in dynamic environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.71443/9789349552982-13\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 3, 4]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "7570b4b436ad70e76755ff47e2cedea92fb50a7f130a2525842fa1417eb0c19e", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_objectives", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.65109/lngi4831", "doi:10.1007/978-3-319-61007-8_2", "doi:10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-pmnmb", "doi:10.71443/9789349552982-13"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.65109/lngi4831", "https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-61007-8_2", "https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-pmnmb", "https://doi.org/10.71443/9789349552982-13"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}

review.alternative: Agents might also rely on fixed heuristics rather than intrinsic curiosity.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that curiosity-driven agents perform worse than fixed-heuristic baselines in novel environments.

claims.statement: Intrinsic motivation (e.g., curiosity) bootstraps exploration in environments with rare or deceptive rewards.

support.explanation: Curiosity enables sense-making by ignoring deceptive external rewards in favor of internal skill acquisition.
support.passage: curiosity-driven learning enables organisms to make discoveries to solve complex problems with rare or deceptive rewards.

review.alternative: Performance gains could be attributed to single-agent scaling rather than multi-agent collaboration.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that single-agent setups outperform the described multi-agent evolutionary baselines.

claims.statement: Multi-agent evolutionary frameworks replace rigid control with collaborative discovery, enhancing open-ended problem solving.

support.explanation: Collaboration through persistent memory allows agents to build upon previous discoveries, scaling discovery rates.
support.passage: CORAL replaces rigid control with long-running agents that explore, reflect, and collaborate through shared persistent memory, asynchronous multi-agent execution, and heartbeat-based interventions.

review.alternative: Non-convex scalarization can be solved via alternative optimization techniques.
review.would_change_mind: A successfully implemented, non-convex robust DICE-based optimization framework.

claims.statement: Existing DICE-based reinforcement learning approaches for objective discovery are constrained by convexity assumptions in their scalarization functions.

support.explanation: The framework cannot handle non-convex objective landscapes due to reliance on Lagrangian duals valid only under convexity.
support.passage: Our formulation assumes convexity, and thus the DICE-based approach relying on the Lagrangian dual does not apply to non-convex scalarization in MORL.

actions.findings:
Intrinsic motivation (e.g., curiosity) bootstraps exploration in environments with rare or deceptive rewards. [source-feb4fddb33664d63]

Multi-agent evolutionary frameworks replace rigid control with collaborative discovery, enhancing open-ended problem solving. [source-91aafd52adc047b4]

Existing DICE-based reinforcement learning approaches for objective discovery are constrained by convexity assumptions in their scalarization functions. [source-4668e4bd26fe43c7]
actions.limitations: Current autonomous objective discovery mechanisms are heavily influenced by the underlying optimization assumptions (e.g., convexity). Effective handling of non-convex scalarization and long-term, self-directed prioritization remains an open challenge.
actions.next_questions: How can intrinsic motivation mechanisms be extended to robustly handle non-convex objective landscapes without compromising exploration efficiency?
actions.reason: Revising findings based on new evidence regarding non-convex optimization constraints and autonomous framework scalability.
actions.summary: Autonomous objective discovery relies on intrinsic motivation and collaborative multi-agent frameworks to bootstrap exploration in environments lacking external reward signals. While these methods achieve state-of-the-art performance in open-ended search, their reliance on specific convexity assumptions limits their applicability to non-convex optimization landscapes, necessitating further development in autonomous goal prioritization.
actions.title: Foundations of Autonomous Objective Discovery in Artificial Systems

proposal.summary: This journal documents the revision of the objective discovery framework, integrating intrinsic motivation mechanisms with multi-agent evolutionary paradigms and acknowledging current limitations in non-convex optimization.
proposal.title: Autonomous Objective Discovery Research Journal
